purpose: Which paragraph properties survive when Word joins two paragraphs through a tracked paragraph mark, and whether the #873 split/merge redline shape resolves correctly under Word Accept All / Reject All.
procedure: Minimal packages (content types, package rels, document.xml only) were opened in Word and resolved with Accept All or Reject All through AppleScript (accept all revisions / reject all revisions), then saved as .docx. Paragraph jc and text were read from the saved document.xml. Revision attributes: w:author="T" w:date="2026-10-19T00:00:00Z".
finding: Removing a paragraph mark (Accept All of a deleted mark, Reject All of an inserted mark) keeps the FOLLOWING paragraph's properties (f1, f2: center, not right). The LibreOffice-derived first-paragraph-survives table in paragraphMergeFormatting.test.ts does not match Word for this case. The #873 shape tracks the changed properties on every part (f3, f4), so the result is the same whichever mark survives.

nvcaSplitMergeSmoke.procedure: For each form, one body paragraph was split at a sentence boundary (joining space removed) and two adjacent body paragraphs were merged. compareDocuments(source, edited) was resolved in Word with Accept All and Reject All; every body paragraph text was compared with the edited and source documents.
